test_title: PYST 54: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 08 Sept, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which major reform was aimed at redistributing land to the landless after independence?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Land Ceiling Acts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Land Ceiling Acts were aimed at redistributing agricultural land to the landless and poor farmers to reduce economic inequality in rural India.
 
• These acts imposed a limit on the maximum amount of land that an individual or family could own, with surplus land being acquired by the state and redistributed to the landless.
 
• Land Ceiling Acts were introduced after independence as part of land reforms to address the concentration of land in the hands of a few landlords.
 
• These reforms were included in the 1st Five-Year Plan (1951-56) and were implemented across various states in India, albeit with mixed success due to loopholes and resistance from landowning classes.
 
• The main aim was to ensure equitable distribution of land resources, increase agricultural productivity, and reduce rural poverty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Crop Insurance Scheme:**

 
 
• The Crop Insurance Scheme refers to initiatives like the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), launched in 2016 to protect farmers against crop loss due to natural disasters, pests, or diseases.
 
• Under this scheme, farmers pay a minimal premium, and the rest is subsidized by the government to ensure financial security for farmers.
 
• It is not related to land redistribution but focuses on mitigating risks faced by farmers in agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Green Revolution:**
 
 
• The Green Revolution began in the 1960s and involved the adoption of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation techniques to increase agricultural productivity in India.
 
• It played a vital role in making India self-sufficient in food grains but had no direct connection to land redistribution.
 
• While it enhanced agricultural production, it also led to regional disparities and benefited mainly large landowners.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Export Policy:**
 
 
• The Agricultural Export Policy, introduced in 2018, aims to increase India’s agricultural exports to $60 billion by 2022.
 
• It focuses on promoting export-oriented farming, ensuring the availability of export-quality produce, and creating a stable trade regime.
 
• This policy is unrelated to land redistribution and primarily deals with enhancing India's position in global agricultural trade.
